title: Question 8
stem:
A neutron within a nucleus decays to produce a proton, a β⁻ particle and an (electron) antineutrino.
n → p + β⁻ + ν̄

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Use the quark composition of the neutron to show that the neutron has no charge.

markscheme_points.text: up/u has charge +⅔(e), down/d has charge -⅓(e)

hints: Hint 1: Identify the given data from the problem and recall the governing equation connecting these quantities using fundamental particles and quarks.
Hint 2: Rearrange the formula to isolate the required quantity before substituting numerical values with correct powers of ten.
Hint 3: Check your intermediate calculation steps carefully and ensure your final answer is stated to an appropriate number of significant figures with correct SI units.
parts.proper_answer: (quark structure is) up, down, down/udd; up/u has charge +⅔(e), down/d has charge -⅓(e); +⅔e -⅓e -⅓e = 0
walkthrough:

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Substitute the known quantities into the formula with correct SI units and powers of ten:
$$(quark structure is) up, down, down/udd; up/u has charge +⅔(e), down/d has charge -⅓(e); +⅔e -⅓e -⅓e = 0$$
Work through the intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
